findings.title: An exception from CleanupHandles skips ExitReadLock, so the global process-start lock is never released.
findings.body: `CleanupHandles` can throw from inside the `finally` block. It throws `Win32Exception` when `SetHandleInformation` fails. It can also throw `ObjectDisposedException`, because it calls `DangerousRelease` before `SetHandleInformation(safeHandle, ...)`; if the caller disposed the handle while the start was running, that release closes it. Either exception skips `ExitReadLock`/`ExitWriteLock` and `commandLine.Dispose()`. After that, every later `Process.Start` that needs the write lock hangs forever. The exception also hides a process that was created successfully, and the rest of `handlesToRelease` is never released. Fix: clear the inherit flag before `DangerousRelease`, don't throw from cleanup (ignore or Debug.Assert the failure), and exit the lock in its own try/finally.

findings.title: One shared ref flag leads to releasing handles that were never AddRef'd.
findings.body: All entries share a single `inheritedHandleRefsAdded` flag. Suppose entry `i` is null or already disposed. Then `DangerousAddRef` throws (NullReferenceException or ObjectDisposedException) after earlier entries set the flag. The `finally` block then calls `DangerousRelease` on every entry, including the one that failed and every entry after it. That either throws from `finally` (null entry) or drops the ref count on a handle this code never ref'd, so a caller's handle can close early or `DangerousRelease` can throw. Fix: count how many refs were added (e.g. `int refsAdded`) and release only `inheritedHandles[0..refsAdded)`. Also skip or reject null entries up front.

findings.title: Under the read lock, concurrent starts can clear each other's inherit flag on a shared handle.
findings.body: Starts that set `InheritedHandles` only take the read lock, so two of them can run at the same time. Suppose both list the same `SafeHandle` (for example, one log pipe shared by several children). When start A finishes, `CleanupHandles` sets HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT back to 0. If start B has already called `SetHandleInformation` but not yet `CreateProcess`, its handle is no longer inheritable. Windows then rejects B's `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST`: CreateProcess fails with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, or the child silently doesn't get the handle. Fix: use the write lock while user handle flags are being changed, or make the flag change reference-counted per handle.

findings.title: EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT and a STARTUPINFOEX-sized cb are now passed to CreateProcessWithLogonW on every credentialed start.
findings.body: `creationFlags` now always includes `EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT`, and `cb` is always `sizeof(STARTUPINFOEX)`. Both now go to `CreateProcessWithLogonW` whenever `UserName` is set, even when `InheritedHandles` is null. As far as I know, `CreateProcessWithLogonW` does not document support for this flag or for attribute lists. If it rejects them, every `Process.Start` with credentials that used to work now fails. If it ignores them, the handle list is silently not applied on that path. I could not confirm from here how the API behaves at runtime. Fix: set the flag and the extended `cb` only when an attribute list is actually used, and only on the `CreateProcess` path. For the logon path, reject `InheritedHandles` or document that it is not supported.

findings.title: POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT closes the child's stdio when no fd is given for it.
findings.body: On the macOS posix_spawn path, `POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT` closes every descriptor that has no file action. Stdio only gets a file action through `adddup2` when `stdinFd`/`stdoutFd`/`stderrFd != -1`. Inherited entries 0–2 are explicitly skipped in the `addinherit_np` loop below. So whenever a stdio fd is -1 (inherit the parent's) and `InheritedHandles` is set, the child starts with fd 0, 1 or 2 closed. The fork path keeps 0–2 open in the same case. I could not see whether the managed caller ever passes -1 here. Fix: when restriction is active, call `posix_spawn_file_actions_addinherit_np` for each STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR_FILENO that has no dup2.

findings.title: An empty handle list is passed to UpdateProcThreadAttribute and makes Start fail.
findings.body: This happens when `InheritedHandles` is an empty list (or holds only invalid or closed handles) and no standard handles are provided (all null or invalid). Then `handleCount` is 0 and `UpdateProcThreadAttribute` gets `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST` with `cbSize` 0. Windows rejects that (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER), so `Process.Start` throws `Win32Exception` exactly when the user asked to inherit nothing. Fix: when `handleCount == 0`, skip the attribute list and pass `bInheritHandles = false` to CreateProcess.

findings.title: CleanupHandles can throw inside finally, so the process-start lock is never released.
findings.body: `CleanupHandles` calls `DangerousRelease()` first and only then calls `SetHandleInformation(safeHandle, ...)`. If the caller disposed the handle while `Start` was running, that release really closes it. Marshalling the now-closed SafeHandle then throws `ObjectDisposedException`, and a failing `SetHandleInformation` throws `Win32Exception`. Either exception comes out of the outer `finally` before `ExitReadLock`. The remaining handles are left AddRef'd, `commandLine` is not disposed, and `s_processStartLock` stays held, so every later write-locked `Process.Start` hangs. Fix: clear the inherit flag while you still hold the reference (call `SetHandleInformation` before `DangerousRelease`), and do not throw from cleanup. Ignore or log the failure so the lock is always released.

held.title: An empty handle list passes cbSize 0 to UpdateProcThreadAttribute.
held.body: Trigger: `InheritedHandles` is set to an empty list (or contains only invalid or closed handles) and no standard handles are supplied (`stdinHandle`/`stdoutHandle`/`stderrHandle` are all null, which this method allows). Then `handleCount` is 0 and `UpdateProcThreadAttribute(PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, ..., cbSize: 0)` is called. Windows may reject a zero-length handle list with ERROR_BAD_LENGTH; if it does, `Process.Start` throws a `Win32Exception` instead of starting with no inherited handles. `Math.Max(1, ...)` protects the allocation but not this call. I have not confirmed the API's runtime behaviour with size 0. Fix: when `handleCount` is 0, skip the attribute list and pass `bInheritHandles = false` to `CreateProcess`.
